answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The saffron multiplier is published, charged in mirror, and dune lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2698 identities would post 2863 proofs and burn roughly 12 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
